323573.title: The characterization of positive graphs
323573.statement:
A graph $G$ is called **positive** if its homomorphism number into every edge-weighted graph is nonnegative. It is called **symmetric** if its vertices can be partitioned into three sets $(S,A,B)$ such that $S$ is an independent set, there is no edge between $A$ and $B$, and an isomorphism between the subgraphs spanned by $S\cup A$ and $S\cup B$ fixes $S$.

**Positive-graph characterization conjecture.** A graph $G$ is positive if and only if it is symmetric.

This conjecture gives a structural characterization of graphs whose homomorphism numbers are nonnegative for every edge-weighted graph, including graphs with negative edgeweights. The paper proves the conjecture for various classes, including all trees, and establishes computationally that it holds for all graphs with at most $9$ vertices; the general case remains open.

325110.title: Multiple-copy Ramsey numbers for loose and tight hypergraph paths and cycles
325110.statement:
Let $R(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})$ denote the Ramsey number for hypergraphs, and let $m\mathcal{F}$ denote the disjoint union of $m$ copies of $\mathcal{F}$. For $k$-uniform hypergraphs, write $\mathcal{P}_r^k$, $\mathcal{C}_r^k$, and $\hat{\mathcal{P}}_r^k$ for the relevant path and cycle hypergraphs.

**Multiple-copy path and cycle conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, $m\geq n$ and $r\geq s\geq 3$,

$$
R(m\mathcal{P}_r^k,n\mathcal{P}_s^k)=R(m\mathcal{P}_r^k,n\mathcal{C}_s^k)=((k-1)r+1)m+\Big\lfloor\frac{s+1}{2}\Big\rfloor n-1,
$$

$$
R(m\hat{\mathcal{P}}_r^k,n\hat{\mathcal{P}}_s^k)=(r+k-1)m+(1+\lfloor\frac{s-1}{k}\rfloor)n-1,
$$

$$
R(m\mathcal{C}_r^k,n\mathcal{C}_s^k)=(k-1)rm+\Big\lfloor\frac{s+1}{2}\Big\rfloor n-1,
$$

and, if $r>s$,

$$
R(m\mathcal{C}_r^k,n\mathcal{P}_s^k)=(k-1)rm+\Big\lfloor\frac{s+1}{2}\Big\rfloor n-1.
$$

The first and third formulas extend the established $k=3$ results and the lower bound for multiple loose cycles; determining whether the natural lower bound is always exact remains open in general, with analogous questions for loose paths, tight paths, and tight cycles.

326074.title: Completeness of compressed plane waves
326074.statement:
Let $\mathbf{w}=(w_1,\cdots,w_d)\in\mathbb{R}_+^d$ define the lattice $\Gamma_{\mathbf{w}}=\{\mathbf{j}\mathbf{w}:\mathbf{j}\in\mathbb{Z}^d\}$. Let $\{\psi^n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be the localized orthonormal modes recursively generated by the displayed variational problems, and define

$$
\mathrm{b}^n_{\mathbf{j}}(\mathbf{x})=\psi^n(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{j}\mathbf{w}),\qquad n\geq1,\quad \mathbf{j}\in\mathbb{Z}^d.
$$

**Completeness of CPWs.** There exists a constant $\mu_0$ such that the set $\{\mathrm{b}^n_{\mathbf{j}}\}_{n,\mathbf{j}}$ generated from the recursive variational definitions is complete for every $\mu\geq\mu_0$. The conjecture concerns whether the compressed plane waves form a complete orthonormal system; the passage explicitly says that this will be studied in future work and provides no resolution.

326449.title: The symmetric doubly stochastic matrix spectral determination conjecture
326449.statement:
Let $\Delta_n^s$ denote the set of symmetric doubly stochastic $n\times n$ matrices, let $\Delta_n^s(a)$ denote the subset with the relevant parameter $a$, let $I_n$ be the identity matrix, let $C_n$ be the matrix defined in the paper, and let $P$ be a vertex of $\Delta_n^s$. For points $X,Y$, write $[X,Y]$ for the line segment joining them.

**Spectral determination conjecture.** For $0<a\leq n$, the only elements of $\Delta_n^s(a)$ that are DS in $\Delta_n^s$ are points on the line segments $[I_n,C_n]$, $[I_n,P]$ and $[C_n,P]$ where $P$ is a vertex of $\Delta_n^s$.

This conjecture proposes a complete description of the elements of $\Delta_n^s(a)$ that are determined by their spectra within the symmetric doubly stochastic matrices, extending the verified case $n=3$.

331382.title: Conjecture on main simple choreographies in the equal mass Newtonian N-body problem
331382.statement:
Let $N\geq 3$ and consider the equal mass Newtonian $N$-body problem. A **main simple choreography** is a simple choreography that is not derived from a given simple choreography by traveling around it multiple times, by a continuation of the angular momentum, or by a combination of both. The trivial circle solution is the rotating $N$-gon.

**Main choreography conjecture.** For every $N\geq 3$, there is a main simple choreography solution different from the trivial circle solution. The number of such distinct main simple choreographies grows rapidly with $N$.

This conjecture arises from numerical discoveries and predicts that the Newtonian problem has many genuinely distinct simple choreographies beyond the rotating $N$-gon. The supplied text does not state a resolution, so its status remains open.

331492.title: Kron-Knuth strengthening of the noncommutative super Schur formula
331492.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the ordered colored alphabet, let $\mathcal{U}$ be the associated noncommutative algebra, let $\mathfrak{J}_
u(\mathbf{u})$ be the noncommutative super Schur function for a partition $
u$, let $\mathrm{CT}_
u^{<}$ denote the colored tableaux indexing the formula, and let $\operatorname{arwread}(T)$ be the associated reading word. Let $I_{\mathrm{Kron-K}}$ be the ideal generated by the stated colored plactic and Kronecker-Knuth relations. **Kron-Knuth conjecture.** For every partition $
u$, one has

$$
\mathfrak{J}_
u(\mathbf{u})=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{CT}_
u^{<}}\operatorname{arwread}(T)\quad	ext{in }\mathcal{U}/I_{\mathrm{Kron-K}}.
$$
 This is presented as a strengthening of the paper's main theorem, and the stated computer checks cover the cases described in the surrounding text; the general assertion remains open.

331493.title: LLT-type Schur expansion conjecture for the stable Kronecker quotient
331493.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}_\varnothing$ be the subalgebra generated by the uncolored variables, let $\mathfrak{J}^\varnothing_
u$ be the corresponding noncommutative Schur function for a partition $
u$, let $\mathrm{SYT}'_
u$ be the specified set of standard tableaux, and let $\operatorname{sqreadLLT}(T)$ be the associated reading word. Let $I_{\mathrm{KR},\leq 3}^{\mathrm{st}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $\mathcal{U}_\varnothing$ generated by the displayed relations with parameter $k=3$. **Stable Kronecker expansion conjecture.** For every partition $
u$,

$$
\mathfrak{J}^\varnothing_
u=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{SYT}'_
u}\operatorname{sqreadLLT}(T)\quad	ext{in }\mathcal{U}_\varnothing/I_{\mathrm{KR},\leq 3}^{\mathrm{st}}.
$$
 The paper presents this as a conjecture related to the Kron-Knuth conjecture and to results of Blasiak, Lam, and collaborators; no resolution is supplied.

332037.title: The combinatorial injection conjecture for dominance order on compositions
332037.statement:
Let $A,a,B,b$ be integers with $A \geq B \geq 0$ and $a \geq b \geq 0$. For $m,n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{U}^m_n$ denote the set of compositions of $n$ with $m$ non-negative parts. For compositions $\lambda$ and $\mu$, write $\lambda\mu$ for their concatenation, and write $\trianglerighteq$ for the dominance order induced by the non-increasing rearrangements. **Combinatorial injection conjecture.** There is an injection

$$
\gamma: \mathcal{U}^A_b \times \mathcal{U}^B_a \hookrightarrow \mathcal{U}^A_a \times \mathcal{U}^B_b
$$

such that, for every $(\lambda_1,\mu_1) \in \mathcal{U}^A_b \times \mathcal{U}^B_a$, if $(\lambda_2,\mu_2)=\gamma((\lambda_1,\mu_1))$, then

$$
\lambda_1\mu_1 \trianglerighteq \lambda_2\mu_2.
$$

This conjecture gives a combinatorial formulation implying the case $k=2$ of the paper's theorem relating total nonnegativity of the matrices $\mathcal{T}_p$ and $\mathcal{S}_p$.

333021.title: Conjecture on 2k-vertex-2-regular-free uniform hypergraphs
333021.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be an integer. An $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph is said to have no $2$-regular subgraphs on $2k$ vertices if it contains no subhypergraph on exactly $2k$ vertices in which every vertex has degree $2$. **The $2k$-vertex conjecture.** There exists $n_k$ such that, for every $n\geq n_k$, every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with no $2$-regular subgraphs on $2k$ vertices satisfies

$$
|H|\leq\binom{n-1}{k-1}+\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{k}\right\rfloor.
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $H$ is a full $k$-star with center $v$ together with a maximal matching omitting $v$. This is motivated by the fact that the proof of the paper's main theorem uses only the absence of such $2$-regular subgraphs, apart from two auxiliary results; its resolution is not supplied in the given text.

333793.title: Multicomplex realization conjecture for QE, QI and FBP complexes
333793.statement:
Let $\Psi$ be an ordered simplicial complex in $QE\cap QI\cap FBP$, with ground set $E$, vertex set underlying a simplicial complex $\Delta$, minimal basis $B_0$, set of bases $\cal B$, internally passive set $IP(B)$ for each basis $B$, and posets $\text{Int}(\Psi)$ and $\text{Gale}(\Psi)$. A multicomplex is a collection of monomials closed under divisibility. Write $m_B\mid m_{B'}$ for divisibility of monomials.

**Multicomplex realization conjecture.** There exists a map $\cal F$ from the class of ordered simplicial complexes in $QE\cap QI\cap FBP$ to the class of multicomplexes such that, for every $\Psi$, conditions (i)--(iv) hold: the variables are $x_i: i$ is a vertex of $\Delta$ not contained in $B_0$; the monomials are in bijection with the bases, with basis $B$ corresponding to $m_B$ of degree $|IP(B)|$ and support $B\backslash B_0$; the poset $\cal M(\Psi)=({\cal B},<_m)$ defined by $B<_mB'$ exactly when $m_B\mid m_{B'}$ extends $\text{Int}(\Psi)$ and is extended by $\text{Gale}(\Psi)$; and if $A\subseteq E$ contains $B_0$, then $\cal F(\Psi|_A)\subseteq \cal F(\Psi)$.

The conjecture is presented as a strengthening of Stanley's conjecture and as a proposed way to add Gale-poset relations to the internally passive poset. The paper proves that it implies Stanley's conjecture, but the supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture itself.

334654.title: Almost-tiling conjecture for the Boolean lattice with copies of a poset
334654.statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, and let $2^{[n]}$ denote the Boolean lattice of subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ ordered by inclusion. A **copy** of $P$ is an induced subposet isomorphic to $P$. For a set $S\subseteq 2^{[n]}$, a partition of $2^{[n]}\setminus S$ into copies of $P$ is a collection of pairwise disjoint copies whose union is that complement.

**Almost-tiling conjecture.** There exists a constant $c=c(P)$ such that for every positive integer $n$, there is a set $S\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ with $|S|\leq c$ such that $2^{[n]}\setminus S$ can be partitioned into copies of $P$.

This is a weaker form of Lonc's exact tiling conjecture and asserts that only a bounded number of elements need be left uncovered, independently of $n$. The supplied text does not state that this weaker conjecture has been resolved.

334813.title: The finite-size component conjecture for the supersymmetric open XXZ chain
334813.statement:
For each $n\geqslant 1$, let $|\psi_L\rangle$ be the zero-energy state of the open XXZ Hamiltonian, and let $A_{\text{V}}(2n+1)$ and $N_8(2n)$ denote respectively the numbers of vertically symmetric alternating sign matrices of size $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ and cyclically symmetric self-complementary plane partitions in a $2n\times 2n\times 2n$ cube. They are given by

$$
A_{\text{V}}(2n+1)=\frac{1}{2^n}\prod_{k=1}^n\frac{(6k-2)!(2k-1)!}{(4k-1)!(4k-2)!},\qquad N_8(2n)=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(3k+1)(6k)!(2k)!}{(4k)!(4k+1)!}.
$$

**Finite-size component conjecture.** For each $n\geqslant 1$,

$$
\frac{(\psi_{2n-1})_{01\cdots 010}}{\lVert\psi_{2n-1}\rVert}=\sqrt{\frac{N_8(2n)}{A_{\text{V}}(2n+1)}},\qquad \frac{(\psi_{2n})_{01\cdots 01}}{\lVert\psi_{2n}\rVert}=\sqrt{\frac{A_{\text{V}}(2n+1)}{N_8(2n+2)}}.
$$

These formulas were inferred from exact diagonalisation through $L=16$ sites and connect special ground-state components with enumerative-combinatorial sequences. Their validity for all $n$ remains unproved in the source.

335806.title: Two-label conjecture for distinguishing indices of regular graphs
335806.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-regular graph, meaning that every vertex of $G$ has degree $k$. The **distinguishing index** of $G$, denoted $D'(G)$, is the least number of edge labels needed so that only the identity automorphism preserves the labeling. **Two-label conjecture.** If $k\geq 5$, then

$$
D'(G)\leq 2.
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform two-label bound for distinguishing regular graphs of degree at least five. The source gives no evidence of a resolution.

344622.title: The distinguishing-index conjecture for connected finite regular graphs
344622.statement: Let $G$ be a connected, finite, regular graph, and let $D'(G)$ denote the least number of colours needed to colour the edges of $G$ so that the only colour-preserving automorphism is the identity. **The regular-graph distinguishing-index conjecture.** Then $D'(G)\leq 2$, unless $G$ is either $K_n$ for $n\leq 5$, $K_{n,n}$ for $n\leq 3$, or $C_5$. This would improve the general bound for distinguishing indices in the regular case; the paper proves the weaker general estimate but presents this sharper assertion as conjectural.

354539.title: Kropholler's conjecture on almost invariant sets and tree actions
354539.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $H$ be a subgroup. A subset $S\subset G$ is **$H$-finite** if it is contained in finitely many right cosets of $H$. Two subsets are **$H$-almost equal** if their symmetric difference is $H$-finite, and a set $A$ is **$H$-almost invariant** if $A$ is $H$-almost equal to $Ag$ for every $g\in G$. Such a set is **proper** if neither $A$ nor $G\setminus A$ is $H$-finite.

**Kropholler's conjecture.** If there is a proper $H$-almost invariant set $A$ such that $A=AH$, then $G$ has a non-trivial action on a tree in which $H$ fixes a vertex $v$ and every edge incident with $v$ has an $H$-finite stabiliser.

This is a relative form of Stallings' Ends Theorem concerning the action of a group on a tree. The source presents the statement as the Kropholler Conjecture and describes the paper as attempting a complete proof, but the supplied status is unknown; the resolution should therefore be checked.

357638.title: Beck's conjecture on parts in odd and distinct partitions
357638.statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer. Count the total number of parts across all partitions of $n$ whose parts are odd, and separately the total number of parts across all partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. A partition has **exactly one even part** when one even integer occurs as a part, possibly with repetition, and no other even integer occurs. **Beck's conjecture.** The excess of the first total over the second equals the number of partitions of $n$ with exactly one even part, possibly repeated. This conjecture relates the partition families in Euler's identity and refines the equality of their numbers by comparing their total numbers of parts; the supplied source does not indicate whether it has been resolved.

360529.title: Gaetz–Pierson's real-rootedness conjecture for identity-pattern character polynomials
360529.statement: Let $k\geq 0$ and let $\lambda$ be a partition. The polynomial $a_{\mathrm{id}_k}^\lambda(n)$ is the character coefficient polynomial associated with the identity pattern of length $k$. **Gaetz–Pierson's conjecture.** For any partition $\lambda$, the polynomial $a_{\mathrm{id}_k}^\lambda(n)$ is real-rooted with all roots less than $k$. This conjecture concerns the root structure of the character polynomials arising from identity-pattern occurrences; its status is not specified in the source.

361335.title: Lazebnik–Verstraëte conjecture on $k$-fold Sidon sets
361335.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_n$ is a **$k$-fold Sidon set** if, for every $c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4\in\{-k,-k+1,\ldots,k\}$ with $c_1+c_2+c_3+c_4=0$, every solution in $A$ to

$$
c_1x_1+c_2x_2+c_3x_3+c_4x_4=0
$$

is trivial in the sense defined in the source. The definition also applies to sets in $[n]$.

**Lazebnik–Verstraëte conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 3$, there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that, for every $n\geq 1$, there exists a $k$-fold Sidon set $A$ in $\mathbb{Z}_n$ or in $[n]$ satisfying

$$
|A|\geq c_k n^{1/2}.
$$

Lazebnik and Verstraëte proved the analogous existence result for $k=2$, while the stated lower bound for every fixed $k\geq 3$ remains conjectural. Such sets are used in the paper's construction related to the constructor–blocker problem.

372417.title: Wang–Feng–Kovács conjecture on maximum intersections of permutation Hamming balls
372417.statement:
For permutations $sigma,pi\tuplein S_n$, let $d(sigma,pi)$ be their Hamming distance, and let

$$
B_r^n(sigma):=brace{\,piin S_n\mid d(sigma,pi)\le r\,}.
$$

For integers $d$ and $r$, define

$$
I(n,d,r):=\maxbrace{\,|B_r^n(pi)cap B_r^n(tau)|:\ pi,tauin S_n, d(pi,tau)=d\,}.
$$

Also define

$$
N(n,r):=\max_{pi,tauin S_n,\,d(pi,tau)\ge 2}|B_r^n(pi)cap B_r^n(tau)|=\max_{d\ge 2}I(n,d,r).
$$

**Wang–Feng–Kovács conjecture.** For any $r\ge 5$ and $n\ge r$, one has

$$
N(n,r)=I(n,2,r).
$$

The quantity $N(n,r)$ is the minimum number of channels needed to guarantee correct decoding of any transmitted permutation with up to $r$ errors per channel. The cited authors established the exact values of $I(n,d,r)$ for $d=2,3,4$ and every $r\ge 2$; the conjecture asserts that, for $r\ge 5$ and $n\ge r$, the maximum intersection is always attained by centers at Hamming distance $2$.

374589.title: Guiduli's spectral dense-neighborhood conjecture
374589.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $T_r(n)$ denote the Turán graph, let $N(v)$ denote the neighborhood of a vertex $v$, let $d(v)$ denote its degree, and let $bb(G)$ denote the spectral radius of $G$. **Guiduli's spectral dense-neighborhood conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda(G)\geq\lambda(T_r(n)),
$$

then either $G\cong T_r(n)$, or there is a vertex $v$ such that

$$
\lambda(G[N(v)])\geq\lambda(T_{r-1}(d(v))).
$$

Furthermore, if

$$
\lambda(G)>\lambda(T_r(n)),
$$

then the conclusion holds for any vertex $v$ having maximum weight given by a positive eigenvector for $\lambda(G)$. The conjecture is presented as a spectral analogue of the dense-neighborhood theorem of Bollobás and Thomason and Erdős and Sós, which proved the corresponding ordinary Turán statement. The supplied text does not state whether Guiduli's spectral conjecture has been resolved.
